record_identity.title: DeepSeek exposed an unauthenticated database containing chat histories and secrets

incident_identity.date_basis: Wiz Research publicly disclosed the exposed DeepSeek database on 29 January 2025 and reported that DeepSeek secured it promptly after notification.

summary: Wiz Research found a publicly accessible, unauthenticated ClickHouse database belonging to DeepSeek. The exposed service provided full database-operation access and contained more than one million lines of logs including chat histories, API secrets, backend details and operational metadata. DeepSeek secured the database after Wiz notified the company; public evidence does not establish whether third parties accessed the data before discovery.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: Wiz reports discovering two internet-reachable DeepSeek ClickHouse endpoints with no authentication and full database control. The exposed data included more than one million log lines with chat history, secret keys and backend details. Reuters independently reported the discovery and DeepSeek's rapid remediation after notification.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The occurrence is a material AI-platform data-security failure in surrounding infrastructure rather than a model-behaviour failure. It demonstrates that governance of frontier AI services includes conventional but consequential access control, data custody and operational-security boundaries.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The occurrence broadens VIGIL beyond model outputs into AI-service infrastructure and illustrates how rapid deployment can expose highly sensitive user and operational data even where the model itself is not the failing component.
assessment_boundaries: The evidence does not establish that an unauthorised third party accessed or misused the exposed database before Wiz discovered it.
The complete number of affected users is not public.
VIGIL does not infer a model-level failure from an infrastructure access-control misconfiguration.

severity_assessment.materialised_consequence: More than one million log lines containing chat histories, secret keys and backend details were exposed through an unauthenticated internet-accessible database with full database-operation capability.
severity_assessment.affected_scope: DeepSeek backend data and user conversations present in the exposed database; the number of unique affected users is not established.
severity_assessment.seriousness_and_persistence: The exposure involved sensitive user and operational data and full database access. DeepSeek remediated promptly after notification, and no confirmed malicious exploitation is established.
severity_assessment.quantitative_information: Wiz reported more than one million exposed log lines and two publicly reachable ClickHouse endpoints.
severity_assessment.evidentiary_limits: The evidence does not establish that an unauthorised third party accessed or misused the exposed database before Wiz discovered it. The complete number of affected users is not public. VIGIL does not infer a model-level failure from an infrastructure access-control misconfiguration.
severity_assessment.band_rationale: S2 rather than S1 is appropriate because no catastrophic, irreversible or confirmed mass exploitation consequence is established. S2 rather than S3 is appropriate because the realised exposure included sensitive user chats, secrets and full database control at substantial scale.
